# Local web stack (HTE): reference

gash hte: a userland Apache and PHP-FPM for local sites with HTTPS, one PHP-FPM pool per site. The guide is [README.md](README.md); this page lists every function, alias and command, as their own help prints it (`gash_help NAME`, `gash COMMAND --help`).

## Commands

### gash hte

```text
gash hte runs a userland Apache and PHP-FPM for local sites: one sudo at
install for the few system steps, everything else as you. The Apache and
PHP-FPM binaries are the ones the system already has.

Every command takes --json (one JSON object on stdout). Errors are the Gash
error envelope on stderr with exit status 1. Without a terminal nothing
prompts: a missing required flag is missing_value, and a destructive step
without --yes is confirmation_required.

Start with: gash hte install, then gash hte migrate (a dry run of what
would move from hte-cli), then gash hte site create. The guide is
docs/hte/README.md; WSL notes are in its "WSL" section.

Usage:
  gash hte [flags]
  gash hte [command]

Available Commands:
  apache      The global Apache overlay and modules
  cert        Site certificates
  doctor      Check the machine and the stack; exits 1 when a check fails
  hosts       The managed block of the hosts file
  install     Install the stack: one sudo for the system steps, then the userland tree, the stack and autostart
  migrate     Move the hte-cli and system vhosts to the stack (a dry-run plan without --apply)
  php         PHP versions and php.ini values
  service     Start, stop and inspect the stack
  site        Create, change and remove sites
  uninstall   Stop the stack, restore the system as install found it, stage the sites for a later install

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for hte
      --json   print one JSON object

Use "gash hte [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### gash hte doctor

```text
Check the machine and the stack: binaries and modules, ports and who holds
them, autostart, the configuration test, every site (HTTP and HTTPS
answers, certificate validity and names), name resolution, the receipt and
the PHP versions. Each failure comes with its remedy. A hosts block that
drifted is written again through the helper. On WSL it also checks that
Windows resolves the site names (see gash hte hosts windows).
Exits 1 when a check fails.

Usage:
  gash hte doctor [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for doctor

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object
```

### gash hte install

```text
Install the stack. install prints its plan, then runs the system steps in
one interactive sudo: the hosts helper and its sudoers line, the low ports
(--ports standard), linger for the systemd unit, and stopping the system
Apache when the plan needs it. Then, as you, it writes the userland tree,
starts the stack and sets up autostart. Running it again changes only what
is missing.

--ports standard binds 80 and 443 (on Linux by lowering
net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start, which lets every local user bind ports
80 to 1023; on macOS directly or through a pf redirect); --ports high uses
8080 and 8443 and needs no port step.
--autostart auto picks launchd on macOS, the systemd user unit where
systemd runs, else none; shell starts the stack from the first interactive
shell that loads gash.
--yes allows stopping the system Apache when the plan does that; while an
enabled system vhost is neither migrated nor excluded, install leaves the
stack stopped and names gash hte migrate.
An uninstall stage is restored when one is found: --restore-stage PATH
names it, --no-restore skips it.

Usage:
  gash hte install [flags]

Flags:
      --autostart string       auto, systemd, launchd, shell or none (default "auto")
  -h, --help                   help for install
      --no-restore             install without restoring an existing uninstall stage
      --ports string           standard (80 and 443) or high (8080 and 8443) (default "standard")
      --restore-stage string   restore the sites of an uninstall stage
      --yes                    allow the destructive steps of the plan (stopping the system Apache)

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object
```

### gash hte migrate

```text
Move the hte-cli and other system Apache vhosts to the stack. Without
--apply it prints the plan (a dry run); --apply runs it and switches the
sites over, and --yes allows stopping the system Apache and archiving the
old vhost files.

--site D migrates only that domain (repeatable); --exclude D or PATH leaves
a domain or a vhost file out (repeatable). --keep-pool-values keeps the old
PHP-FPM pool's PHP values. Certificates are copied; --reissue-certs makes
new ones instead. Each old site keeps its forced-HTTPS behavior.

Usage:
  gash hte migrate [flags]

Flags:
      --apply                 apply the plan
      --exclude stringArray   leave this domain or vhost file out (repeatable)
  -h, --help                  help for migrate
      --keep-pool-values      keep the legacy pool's PHP values
      --reissue-certs         make new certificates instead of copying the legacy ones
      --site stringArray      migrate only this domain (repeatable)
      --yes                   allow stopping the system Apache and archiving the vhosts

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object
```

### gash hte site

```text
Create, change and remove sites. A site is known by its domain; its state,
rendered configuration, PHP-FPM pool, certificate and hosts names follow
from it. Hand edits go in the site's overlay file, which gash never
rewrites.

Usage:
  gash hte site [flags]
  gash hte site [command]

Available Commands:
  create      Create a managed site
  disable     Stop serving a site, keeping its state
  enable      Serve a disabled site again
  list        List the sites
  modify      Change a site (its overlays stay untouched)
  remove      Remove a site: its state, rendered files, pool, certificate and hosts names (never the document root)
  show        Show a site

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for site

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object

Use "gash hte site [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### gash hte site create

```text
Create a site. --domain and --docroot are required (on a terminal a missing
one is asked for); a relative document root is resolved against the current
directory. A flag left out gets its default: HTTPS on, forced HTTPS off,
the loopback bypass off, HTTP/2 on, the dev profile, a www. alias and the
default PHP version of hte.toml (else the newest installed). A value that
is not valid is an error, never replaced by a default.

Each on/off setting has both forms (--https/--no-https, --force-https,
--force-https-bypass, --http2); passing both is conflicting_options.
--force-https-bypass lets plain HTTP through for requests from 127.0.0.1
and ::1. --alias adds a name (repeatable); --extra-http-port and
--extra-https-port add loopback ports to the vhosts (repeatable).

Usage:
  gash hte site create [flags]

Flags:
      --alias stringArray       a name the site also answers to (repeatable)
      --docroot string          the document root (absolute, or relative to the current directory)
      --domain string           the site's domain (its identity)
      --extra-http-port ints    one more loopback port of the HTTP vhost (repeatable)
      --extra-https-port ints   one more loopback port of the HTTPS vhost (repeatable)
      --force-https             redirect HTTP to HTTPS
      --force-https-bypass      do not redirect requests from 127.0.0.1 and ::1
  -h, --help                    help for create
      --http2                   serve HTTP/2
      --https                   serve HTTPS
      --no-force-https          the opposite of --force-https
      --no-force-https-bypass   the opposite of --force-https-bypass
      --no-http2                the opposite of --http2
      --no-https                the opposite of --https
      --no-www                  no www. alias
      --php string              the PHP version (X.Y)
      --profile string          dev, staging or hardened

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object
```

### gash hte site modify

```text
Change a site: only the flags you pass change, the others keep their
values. The flags are those of site create (--docroot is optional here).
Changing the aliases makes a new certificate; --no-https keeps the
certificate so that --https later reuses it. The site's overlay file stays
untouched.

Usage:
  gash hte site modify [flags]

Flags:
      --alias stringArray       a name the site also answers to (repeatable)
      --docroot string          the document root (absolute, or relative to the current directory)
      --domain string           the site's domain (its identity)
      --extra-http-port ints    one more loopback port of the HTTP vhost (repeatable)
      --extra-https-port ints   one more loopback port of the HTTPS vhost (repeatable)
      --force-https             redirect HTTP to HTTPS
      --force-https-bypass      do not redirect requests from 127.0.0.1 and ::1
  -h, --help                    help for modify
      --http2                   serve HTTP/2
      --https                   serve HTTPS
      --no-force-https          the opposite of --force-https
      --no-force-https-bypass   the opposite of --force-https-bypass
      --no-http2                the opposite of --http2
      --no-https                the opposite of --https
      --no-www                  no www. alias
      --php string              the PHP version (X.Y)
      --profile string          dev, staging or hardened

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object
```

### gash hte uninstall

```text
Stop the stack, remove autostart, and restore what install changed, as
its receipt records it (the hosts block, the port setting, linger, the
helper and its sudoers line). Your sites, their certificates and settings
move to an hte-stage-<timestamp> directory that a later install restores.
Document roots are never touched. Needs --yes.

Usage:
  gash hte uninstall [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for uninstall
      --yes    confirm the uninstall

Global Flags:
      --json   print one JSON object
```
